ikam live: WebDAV/watch/CLI edits as put_content + edit_tree, no repack per edit; 400 random edits 0 mismatches, p50 6-35 ms, ~1.2 KB each; live store 24% over repacked (pandas incl.); search 10.6 ms over 46 MB; bench byte-identical, both scores hold

ikam live as a service: --allow-host for a proxy name (still 127.0.0.1 only), IKAM_AUTH basic auth on every request, SIGTERM/SIGINT commit pending edits then exit; fixes edits after repacking an empty store; live bench 0 mismatches; bench exact, north 0.3035, cost 0.2510

option markup_layers (off): office XML parts as skeleton + text members per zip; north 0.3035 -> 0.3005; cases one graph -4.0% (sharing 1.0063 -> 0.9513), multiformat +1.4%, tables -0.2%; cost holds, office repack CPU up; realworld office +0.9% worst

Finder hang on Connecting: webdavfs mount sequence replayed through a Tailscale-like TLS proxy, all correct server side; --log-requests (time, method, path, host, client, status, ms; never the password or query) and UTC times on every live log line

--public (guests read-only; writes, admin, Claude answers need IKAM_AUTH), --max-body 413, --max-store 507, --max-conns 503, 431 header caps; realworld/selftest.py publishes results/latest.json; live bench 0 mismatches, fsck clean
/robots.txt: Allow on --public, Disallow otherwise (was 404), answered before the password check; for web readers that refuse the public test copy

live store grew ~5-14 KB per self-test run: a working tree per edit and files replaced before a commit, never collected; POST /api/gc and --gc-every N (off); selftest check 11 runs gc and reads every file back; ~70% of each run's bytes freed, history kept

full bench on a shallow clone panicked (divide by zero) in repo-history after minutes: its corpora come from pinned commits a shallow clone lacks; now checks each pinned commit's whole history first and exits 2 with git fetch --unshallow; scores unchanged

append-only event log (G graph of sequence labels), idempotency view and last-write-wins kv view from existing objects; April fold tests as laws; every append rebuilt the views (1,000 single appends 6.2 s); scores unchanged
graph_edit re-cuts only the chunks edits fall in (root equals put_graph); views record their log position; 1,000 single appends 6.3 to 3.1 s; objects and bytes unchanged; scores unchanged

Keys::Any for ids and kv (a real 64-bit label-key collision kept and rebuilt); graph_edit reads only its path: one edit at 10M keys 94-105 ms to 2.2-2.4 ms, upper chunks read 1,321 to 3; scores unchanged
GET/HEAD under /dav/results/ send Cache-Control: no-cache (ETag and Last-Modified kept, 304s included): fetchers showed the 02:07 self-test results after the 6:00 run; other files unchanged

Store backends as options (packs, SQLite, LMDB, redb, fjall, RocksDB); packs: 769 MB/s writes, 2 flushes and 2 files per commit (files 66 and 25), 372 MB for 1M objects (files 4.1 GB), open 279 ms at 10M; 500 kills lost nothing; FsStore ref lock no longer wedges after a kill

ingest dropped a group's stored bytes after anti-unifying a new file with it (fill recorded, members read stored bytes): 4 ingests under distinct refs left 149 objects failing fsck; apply_candidate now keeps anything another encoding needs (dictionary, group, Q/M context); no format change

read_range asked the store for a leaf twice (a 4 KiB range of a 1 MB png fetched 2.2 MB, now 1.1); Office ranges rebuild the container (docx 31, pptx 59 reads), one part read by id fetches 2.76 MB against 18.9 MB whole; Markdown sections in groups save nothing
path lookup 2 reads by tree walk, 4 with a path index; db get 10 reads, 2.4 with a chunk cache; incoming links by scan 113k reads and 340 ms, by a reverse view 8 reads and 1 ms (33.9 MB view)
capability check 77 ns, reachable-set check 20 ns, tree-path proof 8 us; 29 internal objects serve 2+ of 24 tenants (one serves all), so checks belong at the file layer
goal search fetches about the matched files (invoice 195 KB, 2.8 ms); 2-character terms read everything (7.3 MB); windows give a model 6x fewer bytes but refetch groups without a cache

ReadSession shares decoded objects across one request's reads: all text files 7.31 to 5.30 MB fetched; goal windows now under the matched files whole (invoice 257 to 166 KB, files 184); 238 Office files 18.9 to 2.68 MB in one session

ingest checked every stored object before dropping a superseded copy, so one view update after a one-file commit read 3.68 GB (16 scans of the store); needed_index keeps that set in memory: 1.9 MB, 546 to 164 ms; same stored objects; off by default (single writer)

the first read of a derived file and any first has_content read all 229 MB of the store (1,907 reads) to build the ledger; the first write then reads 265 MB more for the seed index (2.0 s); a ledger cache would be 159 KB, 0.1 ms to load, but is an on-disk addition

seed_scope bounds the matcher's seed index to some contents' closure: a one-file edit's first write 238 MB / 1.7 s to 0.69 MB / 8.8 ms with the same bytes stored; scoped writes stored 2.9 KB vs 16.2 KB and 8.5 KB vs 21.8 KB (4 candidates per seed fill up on the whole store); off by default

one- and two-byte searches read every file (E127); with a trigram index they now take the posting lists of every trigram holding the pattern plus the contents under three bytes: "Q3" 7.1 MB / 40 ms to 0.70 MB / 12.6 ms, same results; no new structure

one goal end to end (short-term search, windows to a model, edit 5 files, commit, view update): fresh handle 9.22 GB / 2.9 s with defaults, 554 MB / 0.87 s with the recommended options; second goal on the handle 932 MB to 6.3 MB; seed_scope now follows named trees and view chunks (404 KB to 237 KB per view update) and set_seed_scope rescopes a handle
with needed_index on, the ledger's pass over every stored object also builds the needed index, so a fresh handle reads the store once: E133's first goal 554 MB to 324 MB fetched, same bytes written

Store::read_head lets the ledger and needed-index pass fetch 256-byte heads: a fresh handle's first lookup 229 MB to 192 KB with the same requests; the recommended first goal 324 MB to 94 MB, same bytes written

FsStore listings and the seed index in id order, so the same writes store the same encodings in every run and on every filesystem; goal runs now write identical bytes, ingest output and bench bytes unchanged

seed_scope set to the files a goal reads and edits (plus the trees and view chunks it replaces) instead of their folders: E133's first goal 94 MB / 797 ms to 7.7 MB / 318 ms, slightly fewer bytes written

Repo::read_memo (off by default, --read-memo) keeps the stored contents one tree, view or content write reads until it returns: E133's first goal 7.7 MB to 4.5 MB, its view update 3.85 MB to 1.01 MB, next goal 5.7 MB to 3.3 MB, identical objects stored

the recommended goal on real stores: first goal 4.5 MB in 735 ms on files, 351 ms on packs (PackStore::read_head added), 291 ms in memory; on files the view update syncs 425 objects; merges exp/122 so one branch holds all

Grant (src/grant.rs): per goal, read and write byte ranges of named file versions, sealed with keyed BLAKE3; Q3 goal exposes 16.7 KB of 347 KB; edit check 14 to 33 us; refuses all 70 out-of-window edits a file grant allows; reads fetch the same (groups decode whole)

Repo::replace_hints (off by default): with a scope, old trees and view chunks an edit reads join the seed index, so the scope names only the edited files: first goal 4.5 to 2.75 MB, next goal 3.3 to 1.2 MB, first write 1.78 MB to 189 KB, slightly fewer bytes written
ReadSession::search: a goal searches and reads in one session, so the read stage fetches nothing: first goal 2.50 to 2.04 MB, next goal 1.23 to 1.14 MB; 269 KB per goal is the search index load

read_memo also covers template candidates (each similar chunk was read twice per edit): recommended first goal 2.04 to 1.59 MB, next goal 1.14 to 0.78 MB; view update 906 to 522 KB; bytes written unchanged

Repo::object_templates (on by default): off, tree and view chunks are planned only as slices: first goal writes 250 to 86 KB and the store grows less (72 against 76 KB), 332 to 159 ms on packs; edits only add objects

Repo::begin_batch/end_batch/keep_read and ReadSession::into_contents: a goal's writes share one memo, handed the files it read; edit stage 414 to 70 KB, first goal 1.48 to 1.13 MB; the index build now joins the memo; bytes written unchanged
tree and view chunks stored plain: view update reads 405 to 393 KB but writes 72 to 391 KB; five times the growth for 3% fewer reads

Store::stored_len (default reads; Mem, Fs, Pack answer without reading): a batch handed its files reads nothing for template costs; edit stage 70 to 8 KB, first goal 1.13 to 1.07 MB, next goal 744 to 693 KB; writes unchanged

Repo::graph_prefix_pending/graph_node_pending: a view's new edges kept pending, folded every few goals; view update per goal 405 to 22 KB (150 to 37 ms on packs); one fold for two goals reads 445 KB against 744 KB; same final root; smaller view chunks measured and dropped

Repo::exact_short_search (off): patterns of 1-3 bytes answered from trigram postings without decoding; search 655 to 269 KB (index only), same matches; window range reads still fetch whole files (385 KB for 16.7 KB of windows)

seekable frames with a BLAKE3 outboard (measured, not stored): 4 KiB frames halve window reads (Q3 106 to 51 KB) for +55% text storage; 16 KiB frames +11% for 4%; not worth a format addition for small files
Repo::group_size (64 KiB default), --group-size: 16 KiB groups halve a goal's file reads (Q3 385 to 208 KB, AI 82 to 53 KB) for north +2.1% (0.3035 to 0.3100, over tolerance as a default)
search index decoded once per handle and reused (goal.rs config only): next goal 358 to 89 KB, 60 KB with 16 KiB groups; same matches, writes and view root
cutters over 534 text files: paragraph blocks dedup 1.24 (805 shared, fan-out 52); zstd over distinct fragments about 157 KB for every cutter, so cuts are for edits, not storage
new bytes per md edit: whole 740-860, blocks 115-176 (5.6-7.6 refs), CDC 256 201-367, lines 0-101 but 27-30 refs; kernel put_content 139-194
render/1 builtin (a fact) and fragment.rs: put_fragmented, FragmentIndex, propagate; laws in tests/fragment.rs; +145% at rest; option, format addition waits on Eric
renders with short_records: +74% at rest; fan-out 256 edit 69.7 ms against 117 ms
only shared blocks stand alone: +24% at rest, read pass 14.5 ms (plain 17.2); bytes per edit 26-40% below index-rewrite (fan-out 256: 85.6 against 115.3 KB); option, off by default
html: 571/576 blocks local, 72/72 splices exact; docx 0/72 (document-wide bookmark and list ids; 206/236 local once normalised); pdf regenerated (1,049 ms)
propagate_granted checks E140 grants from fragment lengths, no diff: no measured cost (diff check 17.5 ms at 256 files); refusals write nothing; grant 140 B per file, fragment grant would be 57 B
fragment trigram search 0.11 ms against stored index 1.84 ms, exact; after one edit over 64 files indexes update in 1.5 ms reading 101 B (rebuild 42 ms); goal reads 8.0 against 29.2 KB

typed TableIR plus residuals renders csv, json, md byte-exact 24/24 (13/24 csv without cell types); IR 51% of the three formats' bytes; one-cell edit local in every format; 10k rows cost 13-16 KB per edit
FragmentGrant names one fragment: 85 B at any fan-out against 35,772 B per-file at 256 files, same edit time; refusals 0.002 ms, write nothing; sealed format addition, option
docx renderer splices one block (list ids mapped, context style, heading bookmark renamed, zip rewritten as pandoc does): 96/96 whole .docx identical; 35 ms against 65 ms full
put_cut added; plain puts already add ~168 B per one-cell edit at 1k-100k rows (E161's 13-16 KB was FsStore rewrites); rows 10x at rest; groups-64 +45% at rest, 6x faster edits at 100k: option
csv plus residual sidecar stored, json and md rendered on read: -43% on text formats, -1.8% with office files, 24/24 exact; render 241 ms at 10k rows against 6-11 ms read: archive option
bug fix: concat_range rebuilt whole arguments for their lengths; now from the derivation: 100 B range of a 4,096-line render tree 99,064 to 400 decode work; bench bytes, reads, north unchanged
one md edit to html and docx by splices: 58 ms against 134 ms re-render, 72/72 exact; stored as files 2,340 B per edit, html as fragments 3,210 B: store renders plain
ids by position, seams implied, 2 crossing trigrams per seam: 185,690 against 280,615 B, 0.093 ms per query, exact for any pattern length; update 0.24 ms
docx splices for inserted and deleted blocks, headings and lists with bookmarks, list ids and numbering.xml rebuilt: 168/168 whole .docx identical; deletes 2.8 ms against 77 ms
